hints: Divide the derivatives and simplify using $\cos^2t=(1-\sin t)(1+\sin t)$.
Use the given interval to identify the resulting reciprocal cosine as $\sec t$.
walkthrough:
Differentiate $x = t + \cos t$ with respect to $t$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t} = 1 - \sin t$$

Differentiate $y = \ln(1 + \sin t)$ with respect to $t$ using the chain rule:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{1}{1 + \sin t} \cdot \dfrac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(1 + \sin t) = \dfrac{\cos t}{1 + \sin t}$$

Use the parametric derivative rule $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{\mathrm{d}y/\mathrm{d}t}{\mathrm{d}x/\mathrm{d}t}$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\cos t}{1 + \sin t}}{1 - \sin t} = \dfrac{\cos t}{(1 + \sin t)(1 - \sin t)}$$

Expand the denominator and apply the Pythagorean identity $1 - \sin^2 t = \cos^2 t$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \dfrac{\cos t}{1 - \sin^2 t} = \dfrac{\cos t}{\cos^2 t} = \dfrac{1}{\cos t}$$

Conclude with the required trigonometric form:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \sec t$$

hints: Set the gradient from part (i), $\sec t$, equal to 3.
Solve $\cos t=1/3$ for both values of $t$ in $-\pi/2<t<\pi/2$.
For each parameter value, calculate $x=t+\cos t$.
Round the two $x$-coordinates to 3 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Set the derivative $\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$ equal to $3$:
$$\sec t = 3 \implies \cos t = \dfrac{1}{3}$$

Solve for $t$ in the interval $-\dfrac{1}{2}\pi < t < \dfrac{1}{2}\pi$:
$$t = \pm\arccos\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)$$
Evaluate in radians: $\arccos\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right) \approx 1.230959$, so $t_1 = 1.230959$ and $t_2 = -1.230959$.
Calculate the $x$-coordinate using $x = t + \cos t$ with $\cos t = \dfrac{1}{3}$:

State the two $x$-coordinates correct to 3 significant figures:
$$x = 1.56 \quad \text{and} \quad x = -0.898$$
